briefing.opening: Hello everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 24, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis Deepens: Extreme Weather Events and Human Casualties
sections.content: According to a report released today, heatwave-related deaths in Europe this summer have exceeded 50,000, with over two-thirds of these attributed to climate change, anthropogenic warming, or additional heat from fossil fuels [4, 7, 8, 29]. Domestically, late summer heat and torrential rainfall occurred last September, attributed to a rain cloud front advancing 213km further north than usual [1, 6]. As Typhoon 'Champi,' the 30th typhoon of the season, moves northward, the Korean Peninsula is also experiencing the effects of anomalous weather. Flood and storm surge alerts for Jeju Island and the southern coastal areas have been elevated from 'Attention' to 'Caution,' and a heavy rain advisory has been issued [20]. In England, a phenomenon dubbed 'false autumn' has been observed, where trees shed their leaves earlier than usual after a hot summer, indicating a direct impact of climate change [33].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Acceleration of Domestic Climate Change Response and Carbon Neutrality Transition Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, the 'Renewable Energy Day' has been designated as a national commemorative day, and the first government-hosted ceremony was held, expressing a strong policy commitment to expanding renewable energy [3, 15, 16, 19]. Vice Minister Lee Ho-hyeon of the Ministry of Climate also attended the ceremony, emphasizing the government's efforts [15, 19]. Furthermore, criteria for designating 'Just Transition Special Zones' to proactively support regions affected by carbon neutrality have been established, and public feedback on these criteria will be collected until November 2 [11, 14]. Local governments, including Yeongdeok-gun and Hwasun-gun, are continuing their regional energy transition efforts by fostering future energy industries that link nuclear and wind power generation, and by selecting renewable energy public projects [17, 18]. Discussions are also actively underway regarding methods to verify the carbon neutrality reduction effects of the K-GX policy, which involves a total investment of 1,000 trillion Korean Won [9].

sections.title: 🌱 Promoting Climate Action Through Citizen Participation and Expanded Education
sections.content: The importance of civil society participation and education in responding to the climate crisis is being highlighted. The Hongcheon-gun Council for the Baruge Salgi Movement conducted safety culture and climate change response campaigns [2], while the Korea National Arboretum and Kyungpook National University formed a 'Green Alliance' to combat the climate crisis [5]. At the Carbon Neutrality Culture Festival, the importance of resource circulation was emphasized through an upcycling fashion show [10]. Various programs encouraging carbon neutrality in daily life are also being operated, such as 4x carbon neutrality points for using Ziku electric bicycles and a citizen cycling event in Boryeong-si, Chungcheongnam-do [12, 13]. Internationally, efforts to raise awareness through education continue, with climate change being incorporated as a core component in health professional training and 'Teaching Climate Change with Confidence' workshops being held [27, 28].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Change Awareness and Diverse Response Strategies
sections.content: The international community is raising awareness of climate change and exploring diverse response strategies. In the United States, an installation art piece featuring a melting statue of a politician who denied climate change was timed with the midterm election season, raising awareness about climate change [22]. New practical guides on sustainability and climate change in real estate development have been published [24], and discussions continue on the economic aspects of climate change and water stress issues within the United States [25, 30]. Furthermore, climate change is reshaping Indian fiction, leading to the rise of 'cli-fi' (climate fiction) [31]. In Canada, climate change is being discussed as a key issue alongside health and water security in candidate forums, indicating the widespread impact of climate change across society [32]. Scientific efforts also continue, with University of Minnesota researchers contributing to the development of new media for climate change research [26].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the escalating reality of the global climate crisis and the multifaceted efforts, both domestic and international, to address it. This is a time that demands sustained attention and action. This concludes the climate briefing for October 24, 2026.

articles.description: Season will be less vibrant with trees such as birches, which usually offer a striking burst of yellow leaves, already bareAmong a canvas of copper, red and purple autumn leaves on display at Wisley garden in Surrey, south-east England, one tree stands conspicuously naked.“The birch has lost all its leaves,” says Guy Barter, the chief horticulturist at the Royal Horticultural Society. “That’s the effect of drought, so it’ll have no autumn colour this year.” Continue reading...

summary.phenomenon: Trees, including birches, in Wisley Garden, Surrey, southeast England, have shed all their leaves earlier than usual, indicating a less vibrant display of autumn colors this year.
summary.cause: This phenomenon is attributed to the impact of drought following a 'scorching English summer,' which caused trees to shed their leaves prematurely due to stress.
summary.outlook: This autumn, trees such as birches are not expected to display their usual autumn colors, forecasting an overall less vibrant season.
